question: Will AfD win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?

forecasts.reference-class: Baden-Württemberg state-level (Landtag) elections in Germany where AfD has not led seat counts; historically the top seat totals are achieved by CDU or Greens, with AfD typically not the largest party in BW.

sources.claim: INSA poll (16 Oct 2025): CDU 31%, AfD 20%, Grüne 17%.
Infratest dimap poll (16 Oct 2025): CDU 29%, AfD 21%, Grüne 20%.
DIE ZEIT summarises Infratest dimap results: CDU 29%, AfD 21%, Grüne 20%.
BWTrend: AfD ahead of Grünen for second place (Greens around 20%).
Polymarket/AI consensus shows Greens as likely second; AfD around 20% and not leading.
Infratest dimap poll conducted Feb 25, 2026: CDU 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18%, SPD 7%, FDP 6%, Die Linke 5.5%, Others 8.5%; projected seat split places CDU and Greens ahead of AfD.
INSA poll (Feb 2026) shows CDU around 29%, Greens ~21%, AfD ~20%, SPD ~10%, with AfD catching up to Greens but not leading.
INSA/October 2025 poll scenarios described as CDU leading with AfD close to Greens; AfD is not the clear leading party in Baden-Württemberg according to the cited poll.
Official information confirming the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election date (8 March 2026) and that the Landtag consists of 120 seats.

Wikipedia summarizes multiple polling results for Feb–Mar 2026, showing CDU lead or near-lead with Greens, and AfD polling in the teens to high teens; AfD is not consistently the largest party in these western-state polls.
INSA poll (Feb 17–23, 2026) shows CDU 28%, Grüne 22%, AfD 20%, SPD 10%, Linke 7%, FDP 6%, BSW 3%; seat projection CDU 36, Grüne 28, AfD 26.
INSA poll results cited as CDU leading with a narrowing gap; AfD at 20% and Grüne at 22% in coverage of the same polling cycle.
Sw·P reports INSA poll framing with CDU around 28%, Grüne around 22%, AfD around 20% ahead of the 8 March 2026 election.

causal-factors.name: Front-runner effect: CDU maintains lead in polls
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple polls from INSA and Infratest Dimap around late 2025 to early 2026 place CDU at roughly 28–31% with AfD near 18–21% and Greens around 17–22%, making AfD unlikely to top the seat counts.

causal-factors.name: AfD’s position relative to Greens fluctuates but does not exceed CDU
causal-factors.rationale: Even when AfD edges ahead of Greens in some BW-specific readings (e.g., BWTrend), CDU often remains the largest party, limiting AfD’s chances to become the largest seat owner.

causal-factors.name: Western Germany base-rate: AfD rarely leads in BW
causal-factors.rationale: Historical patterns in Baden-Württemberg and other western states show AfD rarely being the largest party, lowering the baseline probability of an AfD seat lead.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets and polls consistently place Greens or CDU ahead of AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Prediction markets (e.g., Polymarket) and multiple polls repeatedly place AfD behind CDU and sometimes behind Greens, reducing the likelihood of AfD winning the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Tail-risk scenario: plausible but weak upside if last-minute shifts favor AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Unforeseen events or turnout dynamics could lift AfD relative to CDU/Greens, but current data imply such swings would be small and insufficient to overcome the lead of the top two.

causal-factors.name: Greens leadership uncertainty (retirement of Kretschmann) could erode Greens support, benefiting AfD indirectly
causal-factors.rationale: Greens gains have been linked to the popularity of Winfried Kretschmann; reports discuss Greens risk of losing ground if he steps back, which could modestly raise AfD’s relative standing. ([polychances.com](https://polychances.com/polymarket-events/baden-wrttemberg-parliamentary-elections-2nd-place/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Infratest dimap Feb 25, 2026: CDU 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18% (AfD not leading)
causal-factors.rationale: Latest Infratest dimap polling shows AfD well behind CDU and Greens, making AfD the unlikely largest party in the Landtag based on current vote shares. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical pattern: AfD rarely leads in Baden-Württemberg and other western states
causal-factors.rationale: Across western German states, AfD has not been the largest party in recent history, which lowers the baseline probability of AfD winning the most seats in BW. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Baden-W%C3%BCrttemberg_state_election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Prediction-market consensus: Greens likely second; AfD around 20% and not leading
causal-factors.rationale: Prediction markets (e.g., Polymarket) show Greens in second place with AfD around 20%, underscoring the low likelihood of AfD surpassing CDU/Greens for the top seat share. ([polychances.com](https://polychances.com/polymarket-events/baden-wrttemberg-parliamentary-elections-2nd-place/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Tail-risk scenario: turnout shifts or events could boost AfD toward 25%+, creating a possible but unlikely path to a first-place result
causal-factors.rationale: There is a nonzero risk that turnout dynamics or disruptive events could lift AfD above the top two, but current polls show limited upside relative to CDU/Greens. ([yahoo.com](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/merzs-cdu-narrowly-ahead-greens-185829979.html?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Current polling lead of CDU/Greens over AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Infratest dimap (Feb 25, 2026) shows CDU ~28%, Greens ~27%, AfD ~18%, indicating AfD is not the largest party in the near term. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Seat projections place AfD well behind the top two (CDU and Greens)
causal-factors.rationale: Projected seats show CDU ~37, Greens ~35, AfD ~24; AfD would need to overtake CDU to win the most seats. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Western Germany base-rate and historical patterns
causal-factors.rationale: Historical patterns in Baden-Württemberg indicate AfD rarely leads; current data consistently show CDU/Greens ahead. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Baden-W%C3%BCrttemberg_state_election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets and contemporary polls indicate AfD is not the leading choice
causal-factors.rationale: Prediction markets (Polymarket) and recent polls place Greens or CDU ahead of AfD, not in the lead. ([polychances.com](https://polychances.com/polymarket-events/baden-wrttemberg-parliamentary-elections-2nd-place/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Greens leadership transition introduces risk to Greens' vote share
causal-factors.rationale: Greens leadership changes (Kretschmann retiring) have been associated with volatility that could erode Green support in BW. ([swp.de](https://www.swp.de/baden-wuerttemberg/umfrage-zur-landtagswahl-bw-cdu-haelt-gruene-auf-distanz-afd-und-linke-auf-dem-vormarsch-78057198.html?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Hypothetical momentum shift where AfD overtakes CDU would raise probability
causal-factors.rationale: Some historical reporting shows AfD closing gaps; a future poll showing AfD leading could materially increase the odds, though such a scenario is not reflected in current data. ([swp.de](https://www.swp.de/baden-wuerttemberg/landtagswahl-2026-gruene-holen-auf-afd-verliert-cdu-stabil-das-zeigt-eine-neue-umfrage-78594088.html?utm_source=openai))
